items.title: Protests after a man dies in hospital
items.text: Thousands of people gathered in Croatia’s capital, Zagreb, on Saturday evening to protest the death of 32-year-old Kristian Josip Periš at a local psychiatric hospital and demand strict accountability . Peris, a former athlete and coach, died on October 21 shortly after being admitted to the clinic. His death sparked widespread public outrage across the country after local media released hospital surveillance footage showing staff holding a pillow over the restrained patient. According to the family’s lawyer, Peris suffered broken ribs and was strangled during an illegal procedure. Protesters in Zagreb, alongside roughly 1,000 demonstrators in the coastal city of Rijeka, carried candles and white pillows and called for better regulation of hospital treatments to prevent similar tragedies. In response, Croatian authorities have arrested several employees and placed four medical technicians under investigation for the aggravated murder of a vulnerable person while prosecutors examine the actions of other staff members. Difficult words: accountability (being responsible for your actions and having to explain them or face punishment), strangled (killed or injured by squeezing the throat so that breathing is stopped), aggravated murder (a more serious category of murder involving extreme cruelty, special circumstances, or a particularly vulnerable victim). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: Protests after a man dies in hospital
items.text: Thousands of people protested in Croatia’s capital city, Zagreb, on Saturday evening after a 32-year-old man died in a psychiatric hospital. Kristian Josip Periš, a former sports coach, died in October shortly after going to the clinic for help. People across Croatia became very angry when local news shared security camera video which showed hospital workers holding a pillow over the tied-up patient. The family’s lawyer said the man was hit, strangled , and had broken ribs . Protesters carried candles and white pillows in Zagreb and the city of Rijeka. They asked for justice and safer hospital rules. Police arrested several workers, and four medical staff are now being investigated for murder while officials question other employees who were there. Difficult words: tied-up (bound or fastened with rope, straps, or similar material to prevent movement), strangled (when someone squeezes a person’s neck so that they stop breathing), rib (one of the curved bones which protect the chest and its organs). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Protests after a man dies in hospital
items.text: Thousands of people protest in Zagreb, Croatia, on Saturday evening. A 32-year-old man dies in a psychiatric hospital . This man is called Kristian Josip Periš. He is a famous athlete. Kristian Josip Periš goes to the clinic for help in October. But he dies there. People get very angry. They see security video of hospital workers. They are holding a pillow over his face for seven minutes. They are hitting the man. Protesters bring candles and white pillows to the streets in Zagreb and Rijeka. They want justice and better rules for hospitals. Police arrest several hospital workers. They speak to four people because of a murder. Difficult words: psychiatric hospital (a place for people who have mental problems), security video (video by cameras inside a building or area), justice (when things are fair and according to rules). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Art brings people together
items.text: As part of the 2026 Year of Culture, artists and designers from Qatar, Mexico, and Canada are collaborating across borders to share traditions, creative techniques, and personal stories. Mexican designer Fernando Laposse traveled to Doha for his exhibition, The Sower , which blends Qatari pearls with Mexican natural dyes and explores how ancient farming knowledge and seeds can help communities adapt to harsh climates. Meanwhile, Qatar-based designer Yasamin Shaikhi visited Mexico to work with local artisans. She combines traditional ceramics and metalwork with her experimental designs and discovers surprising similarities in their artistic patterns. At MIHAD, a new contemporary gallery in Doha, Canadian photographer Joanna Johnston is displaying personal photographs of Alberta’s prairies taken during a trip with her late father. She uses visual storytelling to connect with local audiences. Ultimately , these cross-cultural exchanges demonstrate that art can bridge geographical divides and create lasting inspiration and friendships long after the exhibitions close. Difficult words: blend (to mix or combine different substances, styles, or ideas smoothly so they form a unified whole), contemporary (modern in style or design), ultimately (finally). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: Art brings people together
items.text: Artists and designers from Qatar, Mexico, and Canada are working together during the 2026 Year of Culture to share their traditions and creative ideas. Mexican designer Fernando Laposse brought an exhibition to Doha. He mixes Mexican natural colors with Qatari pearls and studies how traditional farming can help plants survive dry weather. In turn, designer Yasamin Shaikhi traveled from Qatar to Mexico to make pottery and metalwork with local craftspeople. He found many similar patterns between their two cultures. At a new art gallery in Doha, Canadian photographer Joanna Johnston is showing personal pictures of the open fields in Alberta that she took on a special trip with her father. Through these projects, the artists show that creativity brings people from different parts of the world closer together and builds lasting friendships. Difficult words: creative (using imagination to produce new ideas), pottery (pots, dishes, and other objects made from baked clay), pattern (a repeated design, or shape). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Art brings people together
items.text: Artists from Qatar, Mexico, and Canada are sharing their art and culture in 2026. Fernando Laposse is a designer from Mexico. He goes to Qatar with an art show. He uses Mexican plant colors and pearls from Qatar. He also studies how old farming ways can help plants grow in hot weather. Designer Yasamin Shaikhi goes from Qatar to Mexico. She makes art with local workers. They found many similar ideas. In Qatar, Canadian photographer Joanna Johnston is showing photos of nature in Canada. She takes these photos with her father. These artists show that art helps people from faraway countries understand each other and become friends. Difficult words: designer (a person who plans how something will look), pearl (a small white ball from inside a shell), faraway (long way off). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Governments asking people to prep for emergencies
items.text: European governments are asking people to prepare for emergencies by keeping enough food and water to survive for 72 hours. The UK, France, Ireland, and the Netherlands have provided information to encourage people to prepare for possible disasters. The UK's campaign has a simple name. It is called "Be Ready". It advises families to store bottled water, canned food, a wind-up radio, and sleeping bags. The advice is changing people's shopping habits. Sales of bottled water in the UK have risen by 67 per cent, while sales of canned food have increased by 37 per cent. A London shop owner said: "There is an uplift, 100 per cent." He said he is selling a lot of torches and camping cookers. Governments are worried that events could stop people from getting things they need. These events include extreme weather, like heatwaves, storms, and wildfires. In addition, cyberattacks could affect supermarkets, electricity networks, and other important services. Recently, cyberattacks on European supermarkets caused problems with refrigerators and freezers. Stores had to throw away large amounts of frozen and chilled food. Other events, such as computer system failures, could also stop people using the internet or accessing cash. The UK government said people should take "simple steps" to be ready. items.title: U.S. brings an end to production of one-cent coin
items.text: The United States has officially brought an end to the production of its one-cent coin. President Donald Trump signed the Common Cents Act on Friday. However, the coin will remain legal tender and continue circulating. The US Mint had actually stopped manufacturing the penny (the nickname for the coin) in November 2025. Businesses now have to round cash transactions up or down to the nearest five cents when exact change is unavailable. The decision to discontinue minting the penny was an economic one. In 2024, each coin cost 3.69 cents to produce. The bill's author, Lisa McClain, said: "This legislation will save $85 million per year by permanently ending penny production. It's common sense." The penny's history dates back to the founding years of the United States. Congress established the US Mint in 1792. The following year, the mint distributed more than 11,000 one-cent coins. The penny underwent numerous design changes. Early designs included an image of Liberty, a Native American chief's headdress, and an eagle. In 1909, it featured a portrait of former President Abraham Lincoln to commemorate the centenary of his birth. The last major redesign was in 2010. Rising manufacturing costs gradually undermined the coin's viability, consigning it to history. items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 is released worldwide
items.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) has finally been released. Millions of video game fans worldwide are now playing it. They have waited 13 years for a new GTA game since the release of GTA 5. Gaming experts say the latest version could be the biggest entertainment release in history. It has already sold millions of copies, and it is set to make billions of dollars. Some fans are so excited that they are taking days off work or school to play it. An HR company in the UK said that workers in Britain booked around 83,000 days off because of the game. Many fans tried to make their games consoles think they lived in New Zealand by changing their region settings. They tried this so they could play the game earlier. GTA 6 has received excellent reviews for its high-quality, realistic graphics and exciting story. Players get to explore a huge world of crime and follow the lives of two criminals. However, many experts warn that the game is unsuitable for children under the age of 17. That is because it contains violence, killing, car theft, bad language, drugs, alcohol and sexual content. Media expert Jasmine Hood Miller said: "In GTA, players commit crimes, sometimes against ordinary people who did nothing wrong." She added: "GTA is a very well-made game that teens find fun to play." items.title: Wire upgrade at fault for grounding all US flights
items.text: Thousands of flights across the USA were grounded on Friday the 13th following a major communications failure in the country's air traffic control system. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop after problems with radar and communications equipment. More than 3,500 airplanes were in the air at the time. Thousands of flights were cancelled, leaving passengers stranded at airports nationwide. The problem was eventually traced to an overloaded router, possibly as a result of maintenance work to replace decades-old copper wires with fibre-optic cables. The FAA lifted the ground stop almost five hours later. Operations may take days to return to normal. The incident sparked widespread concern. Officials quickly reassured the public that it was not another 9/11. The US homeland security secretary said there had been no indication of a cyberattack or national security threat. He described the incident as a "telecommunications outage". Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed the failure on outdated infrastructure. He said: "We have old switches and old routers. We use 1980s little copper lines." He added: "It's an old system that went down. It went down everywhere. It got overloaded." Duffy warned that systems would "continue to break" unless Congress allocated extra funds. He said: "I can't build things if I don't have money." items.title: Cuddlers help babies
items.text: For over 35 years, Rush University Medical Center in Chicago, USA, has been helping infant patients and their families through a volunteer cuddler program. When families are away from the hospital’s neonatal intensive care unit (NICU), volunteers comfort infants with cuddles. Families can’t be in the hospital all the time, but the babies had needs after they left. The staff understood these needs, and volunteer cuddlers helped. A lot of the volunteers are parents whose children were in the NICU before. After undergoing extensive training, they are using their experiences and skills to provide other parents a sense of relief and security. Studies show that interactions like holding, rocking, singing, reading, and talking to the infants reduce stress and pain, and they improve their overall physical health. Difficult words: infant (a very young child), neonatal (newborn children), comfort (to make someone feel better). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: Cuddlers help babies
items.text: More than 35 years ago, workers at a medical center in Chicago, USA, thought about how they could help babies. Parents were sad at the hospital’s neonatal intensive care unit . They couldn’t be with their babies all the time. The hospital staff knew that babies needed someone’s care when their parents weren’t there. The children felt better and they were healthier when someone held them, sang, and talked to them. Volunteers took special training to learn how to cuddle the babies and make them feel better. Many of the volunteers were parents whose babies also spent time at the unit. Thanks to the volunteers, other parents didn’t feel guilty when they had to leave because they knew that someone else helped their child. Difficult words: neonatal intensive care unit (a special area of the hospital where staff look after newborn babies), volunteer (a person who does work for no money), guilty (when a person feels bad that he did something wrong). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Cuddlers help babies
items.text: A neonatal intensive care unit is a place in the hospital. Very young babies are there. The staff must look after them all the time. Parents stay with the children, too. They cannot be there all the time. They feel bad about it. The staff get an idea at a medical center in Chicago, USA. They start a volunteer cuddler program. This program starts 35 years ago. People in this program get special training. They learn how to cuddle babies. They learn how to make them feel good. Many of the volunteers are parents. Volunteers cuddle the babies. They sing and talk to them. Studies show that these babies feel better. They are healthier. Their parents feel better, too. Their children are not alone. Difficult words: staff (all the people who work in one organization), volunteer (a person who works for no money), cuddle (to hold someone for a long time in a loving way). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: COP31 brings no deal
items.text: The United Nations COP31 climate talks in Turkey failed to reach a major new agreement to tackle global warming. Although negotiations were extended late into Sunday, which made it the longest UN climate conference in history, deep divisions over fossil fuels and financial aid prevented a deal. The EU, the UK, and vulnerable Pacific island nations rejected the final draft text because oil-producing countries blocked any mention of transitioning away from fossil fuels, the primary driver of climate change. At the same time, African and developing nations objected to the lack of clear financial commitments from wealthy countries to help them adapt to extreme weather and rising sea levels. Conference leaders and campaigners warned that the collapse represents a serious blow to global cooperation, and urged wealthy nations to show stronger leadership, limit the influence of fossil fuel lobbyists , and deliver real climate finance. Difficult words: vulnerable (likely to be harmed, damaged, or negatively affected), primary driver (the most important factor or force that causes something to happen or develop), lobbyist (a person who takes part in an organized attempt to influence legislators or officials to support a particular interest or industry). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: COP31 brings no deal
items.text: COP31, the United Nations climate conference in Turkey, ended without a new agreement because countries couldn’t agree on fossil fuels and money. The meeting lasted longer than any previous climate conference as leaders tried to find a solution . The EU, the UK, and small island nations refused to accept the final plan because it didn’t mention stopping the use of fossil fuels, which causes global warming. At the same time, poorer countries in Africa and elsewhere were angry because rich nations didn’t promise enough money to help them deal with floods, heat waves, and rising oceans. Many experts and activists said the failed talks are a big problem for the world and asked rich countries to take stronger action against climate change. Difficult words: previous (the one before now), solution (the way of solving a problem or dealing with a difficult situation), refuse (to say no). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: COP31 brings no deal
items.text: There is a big United Nations meeting about climate change in Turkey. It is called COP31. It ends with no deal. Leaders from many countries talk for many days. But they can not agree . European countries and small island nations say no to the final plan . It does not talk about stopping oil, gas, and coal, which make the Earth warmer. Poorer countries are also unhappy. Rich countries do not promise money to help them with bad weather and rising seas. Many people are disappointed . They say that world leaders must work harder to save our planet and help poor nations. Difficult words: agree (to have the same idea; to say yes), final plan (the last version of a deal), disappointed (sad because something does not happen the way you wish). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Trump calls Putin his friend
items.text: US President Donald Trump is defending his recent trilateral summit in China with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, even though the high-profile meeting produced few concrete results and left American allies unsettled . At a news conference on Friday, Trump described Putin as his friend and insisted that their personal relationship could help end Russia’s ongoing war in Ukraine. However, Trump declined to say whether Putin acts as a friend to American interests. He stated that ending the conflict is extremely difficult and blamed both sides for not knowing how to stop it. Shortly after the summit, Trump also called into a meeting of European leaders and reportedly questioned their continued support for Ukraine, right as fresh Russian strikes damaged European embassies in Kyiv. Despite Trump’s claims of progress, analysts note that Putin has shown no sign of wanting peace and no peace deal is any closer. Difficult words: trilateral (involving three groups, parties, or countries), unsettled (anxious, uneasy, or worried about a situation), decline (to refuse to accept, do, or answer something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: Trump calls Putin his friend
items.text: US President Donald Trump is defending his recent meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in China. Although the meeting brought together the world’s three biggest powers, it achieved very few real results and worried America’s European allies . At a news conference on Friday, Trump called Putin his friend and said their good relationship could help stop the war in Ukraine. Trump could not say if Putin is a friend to the United States, though. Soon after the meeting, Trump spoke to European leaders and questioned why they continue to support Ukraine, even as new Russian attacks hit buildings in Kyiv. Critics point out that Putin started the invasion and shows no real signs of stopping the war, which means Trump is still far from making a peace deal. Difficult words: ally (a country or organization that formally cooperates with and supports another, especially in politics or war), question (to express doubt about something, or to ask someone questions to get information), invasion (coming to a country or region with an armed force). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
